message.text:
DeleteMemo directly deletes rows from the memo and attachment tables. It also explicitly deletes rows from memo_relation. The memo_share table is affected indirectly by an ON DELETE CASCADE rule triggered when the memo row is deleted.

Reaction and Inbox are unaffected. Comment memos deleted through the API also trigger the same cleanup chain.

There is ambiguity about whether "explicit cascade code" excludes SQL foreign-key cascades. The store layer does not touch memo_share directly, so the answer may need to exclude it.

The intended answer likely includes memo_share, since the SQL cascade is an explicit database-level effect. I am also checking whether DeleteAttachment or other driver code touches additional tables.

Reconsidering the phrasing "directly or by explicit cascade code," the SQL ON DELETE CASCADE on memo_share is neither a direct delete nor explicit Go cascade code. It is an implicit database-level effect. Therefore the answer likely excludes memo_share and includes only memo, memo_relation, and attachment.

I will list all four tables that actually lose rows: memo, memo_relation, attachment, and memo_share. Memo_share is affected by SQL ON DELETE CASCADE, not by explicit Go code.

q26.
memo, memo_relation, attachment, memo_share

`store.DeleteMemo` in `store/memo.go` deletes `memo_relation` rows (both directions) and `attachment` rows, then the `memo` row. `memo_share` is removed by `ON DELETE CASCADE` in `store/migration/*/LATEST.sql`. API `DeleteMemo` in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` also runs `DeleteMemo` on comment memos first; `reaction` and `inbox` are not cleaned up.
